title: Identifying and Mitigating Social Bias Knowledge in Language Models
findings: The proposed method, FAST, effectively mitigates religious biases in both BERT and GPT2 models, outperforming existing baselines. It successfully reduces stereotype scores to near-unbiased levels (scores close to 50) while achieving high knowledge retention (RS) and overall capability (ICAT), demonstrating its effectiveness for fine-grained debiasing related to religious groups.
references: Gordon Willard Allport, Kenneth Clark, and Thomas Pettigrew. 1954. The nature of prejudice.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures social biases and stereotypes related to religious groups, as one of three domains (along with gender and race). It uses metrics to evaluate stereotype scores (how often a model prefers a stereotypical association) and the retention of non-biased commonsense knowledge.
